title: Nuevo Laredo Schools to Ban Student Cell Phones Starting Tuesday, November 3

content:
Starting tomorrow, Tuesday, November 3, basic-education schools in Nuevo Laredo will begin enforcing a rule banning students from using cell phones during the school day, according to Noticias de la Frontera.

Secondary school directors confirmed they recently received the official circular and have already communicated the measure to parents, who are expected to help ensure compliance.

Juan Manuel Medina Rentería, director of Secundaria Técnica 57 “Santiago M. Belden” in the Las Torres colonia, said his campus is prepared to implement the rule, though he acknowledged some students may resist because they are accustomed to using their devices for much of the day.

In many cases, Medina Rentería said, phones are not used for educational purposes but to access social media, create content and chat during school activities. As part of the measure, parents must sign a letter stating they are aware of the ban.

If a student is caught using or carrying a phone in violation of the rule, the device will be held and returned at the end of the school day, after a report is filed and the parent or guardian is notified — and the parent must come to the campus in person to pick it up. No suspensions are planned for this infraction, Medina Rentería said; instead, the school will involve parents directly so they supervise that their children do not bring phones to school.

To avoid communication problems, Secundaria Técnica 57 will keep its landline available so students can reach family when needed, and parents will have the campus phone number for any unexpected situation. The rule aims to cut classroom distractions and support academic performance, amid concerns about excessive device use among children and adolescents, linked to concentration difficulties, fatigue and effects on emotional well-being.
